transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side of my face looks. I work in computer support, so I'm on video calls a lot, and I also do salsa dancing, and whenever I see myself on screen or in photos, it's just so obvious to me. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, but it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life. It's just getting too hard to deal with.
Do thoughts about the left side of your face keep popping into your mind even when you try not to think about it?

Yes, they do. Like I was saying, I really just can't stop focusing on it. I'll try to push it out of my head while I'm working, but the second I'm on a video call, or if I see a photo from salsa dancing, the thoughts come right back. It's just... always there. Even though my friends and family keep telling me they don't see the puffiness or the unevenness, I just can't turn my brain off about it. It's really interfering with everything.
Do you think it’s possible that the problem with your face is not as noticeable as it feels to you?

I mean... I guess it's possible. Logically, I know everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything. But to me, it just doesn't feel that way. 

Like I said, when I'm on a video call or looking at those salsa photos, I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side of my face looks. It's just so glaring to me. So even if other people really don't notice it as much, it doesn't change the fact that I can't stop seeing it, and it's still really messing up my work and my social life.
Are you absolutely certain that the left side of your face is actually uneven and puffy?

Well, I... I'm not 100 percent sure, I guess. I mean, I see it clearly, but since literally everyone else says they don't, there's a part of me that wonders if maybe I'm seeing it wrong. But it just feels so real to me when I look in the mirror or at a screen. So, no, I'm not absolutely certain, but it's hard to shake the feeling that it's there.
Do you spend a lot of time checking the left side of your face in mirrors, photos, or on camera?

Yes, I do. It actually takes up a lot of my time. Um, especially right before work meetings or if I'm getting ready to go out somewhere. I'll just keep opening the camera preview on my computer or my phone, and... I just sit there changing the angle and the lighting. I'll keep fixing my hair, trying to get it to fall right around that side of my face to hide it. 

If it's a photo, I'll retake it over and over. And I'm constantly asking my friends if I look strange. I just get stuck doing all of this until I end up running late to whatever I'm doing, or I'm honestly just too drained to even go out anymore.
Have you ever been completely convinced that the left side of your face is definitely abnormal, even when other people tell you it isn’t?

No, I don't think I've ever been completely, one hundred percent convinced that it's abnormal. I mean, like I said, I see it, and it really bothers me, but... because everyone else tells me they don't see it, I've always had that bit of doubt. I've never thought they were lying to me or that I was the only one seeing the absolute truth. I just... I see it, and it feels real to me, but I know they don't. So, no, I wouldn't say I've ever been completely convinced.
Do you also have unwanted thoughts about things other than your appearance that make you feel driven to do repeated rituals or checking?

No, not really. I mean, it's pretty much just my face that I get stuck on. I don't have, like, a need to wash my hands a certain number of times or check the stove over and over. It's just the mirror checking and the camera stuff with my appearance. So, no, I don't really have thoughts like that about other things.
